<!--
  HOW TO FILL THIS FILE — read before tagging a release
  =======================================================
  This file is read by .github/workflows/build-release.yml when you push a
  tag (e.g. `v1.4.0`). Each section below gets copied straight into the
  generated GitHub Release notes (dist/RELEASE_NOTES.md).

  RULES:
  1. Section headers must be on their own line, exactly as shown below.
     Matching is case-insensitive, so "new features", "New Features", and
     "NEW FEATURES" all work.
  2. "Improvements" also accepts the header "Updates" — either works.
  3. Under each header, add one Markdown bullet per line, e.g.:
       - **WiFi:** Fixed driver crash on RG351MP after resume from sleep.
     Bold the short tag (feature/device/area), then describe the change.
  4. Leave a section's bullets empty (or delete the bullets, keep the
     header) if there's nothing to report — the workflow will automatically
     fall back to a generic "Placeholder" bullet for that section so the
     release notes don't look broken.
  5. "Full Changelog" is a single optional line for a GitHub compare link,
     e.g.:
       **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/compare/v1.3.0...v1.4.0
     Leave it blank and the workflow will auto-generate the compare link
     from the previous git tag automatically (see workflow patch).
  6. THIS FILE IS NOT RESET AUTOMATICALLY. Update it yourself before every
     tag push — otherwise old notes from the last release will carry over
     into the next one.
-->

- TEST NEW FEATURES
